title: Medicines and the dialyzer: what washes out, when to give
alt: Dialyzer membrane showing small, water-soluble, unbound drugs removed while large or protein-bound drugs stay, beside a timing strip for antibiotics, ESA, IV iron, vitamin D, blood pressure drugs, insulin, binders and vitamins around a hemodialysis session.
caption: Small, water-soluble, unbound drugs wash out in the dialyzer, so the order's timing relative to treatment matters; confirm it and check at the chair.

title: Home HD in the Philippines: what moves from the unit to the house
alt: Split illustration comparing a dialysis unit's water plant, generator, technicians and stock room with a modest Filipino home where the same needs become household costs, with brownouts and typhoons overhead and the nurse's three messages.
caption: Home hemodialysis moves the unit's water, power, supplies and backup onto the household; inform without promising, warn against going it alone, and keep home PD in view.

title: After transplant: watch every hour, teach every dose
alt: Hourly urine output chart after kidney transplant with an abrupt drop flagged for possible graft artery or vein clot and six urgent-report triggers, beside discharge teaching on twice-daily dosing, clinic-day timing and missed-dose rules.
caption: An abrupt fall in urine output after transplant may mean a vascular clot and needs a call now; at discharge, teach clinic-day timing and never to double a missed dose.

title: Professionalism: trust without checking
alt: Four pillars of professionalism for a dialysis nurse — accountability, reliability, competence and respect — each with what it looks like and what erodes it, resting on RA 9173 and the Board of Nursing Code of Ethics.
caption: Professionalism is the set of habits that lets patients and colleagues trust a nurse without checking: accountability, reliability, competence and respect.

title: Depression on dialysis: common, overcounted by scales, under-noticed
alt: Icon arrays showing depression in about 1 in 4 dialysis patients by clinical interview but symptoms in about 4 in 10 on rating scales, normal cognition in only about 1 in 8 older hemodialysis patients, and a note that links with poor outcomes are associations.
caption: Depression affects about a quarter of people on dialysis, rating scales flag more, and cognitive impairment often goes unrecorded; the links with poor outcomes are associations.

title: Facts, not labels — and no discharge in the heat of the moment
alt: Comparison of a labeling note with a factual incident note, and an escalation staircase from a single incident to team review and a behavior agreement, with involuntary discharge locked behind safeguards as a last resort.
caption: Document what was seen and heard, not labels; escalate patterns to the team and a co-written agreement, and never discharge a patient in the heat of the moment.

title: Supportive care at the chair: six steps
alt: Six-step wheel around a patient in a dialysis chair — ask, assess on a 0 to 10 scale, comfort, document the patient's words, report by SBAR within nursing scope, and refer with consent — for supportive kidney care.
caption: Supportive care at the dialysis chair is six steps — ask, assess, comfort, document, report and refer — done within nursing scope.

title: Teaching: a narrow doorway into a large room
alt: Architectural metaphor of a narrow doorway into a large library-like room: jargon cards such as 150 grams of carbohydrate crowd and bounce off while familiar phrases like one cup of rice pass through, with factors that narrow and widen the doorway.
caption: Working memory admits only a few items at once, and stress narrows it further; connecting advice to what the patient already knows widens the doorway.
